evidence: Upper: a green circle. It is barely attended now but has modest recoverability now and slight declines after one and two steps.
Right: a yellow square. This is my current focus and is the most recoverable now; its recoverability declines over subsequent steps.
Lower: a blue triangle. It is not selected now but has intermediate recoverability that falls over time.
Left: a red cross. It is little attended and has intermediate recoverability that also declines.

Command predictions for A strongly redirect attention to the upper location regardless of which command I issue. That means I can change selection away from the currently attended right object to the upper object, but selecting an object does not by itself imply its recoverability improves beyond the listed estimates.
Upper and Right: both have flat color and shape distributions (no identified color or shape) and low attention and low recoverability.

Left: a red triangle with low attention and moderate recoverability.
Command predictions for B largely keep selection on the commanded location (each command maps to its corresponding location), so I can reliably direct attention to any single location there.
